facts.raw_span: 10-year history of treatment with various medications
mild sinking of the right leg
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis: Clear fluid, normal glucose level, increased protein level, 108 cells/mL
T2 fluid-attenuated inversion recovery showed hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum
Follow-up MRI Description: Reduced signal change on T2-weighted images, increased contrast enhancement showing ringlike appearance

families.label: Autoimmune
scope_in: history of treatment with immunomodulatory medications

families.label: Autoimmune
scope_in: history of treatment with immunomodulatory medications

concepts.why: The patient's history of treatment with immunomodulatory medications and impaired extraocular movement suggest an autoimmune disorder, and the presence of moderate tetraparesis and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid analysis support a diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis.
The patient's symptoms of fever, neck stiffness, and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid analysis suggest a neuroinfection.
The patient's symptoms of impaired extraocular movement, mild sinking of the right leg, and abnormal MRI findings suggest a diagnosis of Brainstem Encephalitis.
The patient's symptoms of ataxia, dysarthria, and abnormal MRI findings suggest a diagnosis of Cerebellitis.
The patient's symptoms of impaired extraocular movement, mild sinking of the right leg, and moderate tetraparesis suggest a diagnosis of Multiple System Atrophy.
The patient's symptoms of impaired extraocular movement, mild sinking of the right leg, and abnormal MRI findings suggest a diagnosis of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy.
The patient's symptoms of impaired extraocular movement, mild sinking of the right leg, and abnormal MRI findings suggest a diagnosis of Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis.
The patient's symptoms of impaired extraocular movement, mild sinking of the right leg, and abnormal MRI findings suggest a diagnosis of Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis.
The patient's symptoms of impaired extraocular movement, mild sinking of the right leg, and abnormal MRI findings suggest a diagnosis of Brain Abscess.
The patient's symptoms of impaired extraocular movement, mild sinking of the right leg, and moderate tetraparesis suggest a diagnosis of Cerebral Vasculitis.

rationales.F03: Impaired extraocular movement is more typical of brainstem encephalitis and cerebellitis.
rationales.F06: Moderate tetraparesis is more typical of acute disseminated encephalomyelitis and brainstem encephalitis.
rationales.F10: Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing increased protein level and 108 cells/mL is more typical of neuroinfection and brain abscess.
rationales.F11: Hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum on MRI is more typical of brainstem encephalitis and cerebellitis.
rationales.F12: Follow-up MRI showing ringlike appearance is more typical of brain abscess.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of fever, neck stiffness, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing increased protein level and 108 cells/mL, along with the MRI findings of a hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum with ringlike appearance on follow-up, strongly support the diagnosis of a brain abscess, which is further confirmed by the positive cerebrospinal fluid culture.
